title: By time
hookLine: by time, humanity is in loss, except those who believe, do good, and urge truth and patience (Quran 103)
tomorrow: what if the silence goes on, and it feels like you've been left?

lines: MAN IS IN A STATE OF LOSS.
cards: The weekly screen-time report lands on a Sunday morning: a number nobody chose on purpose. The Quran has a surah of three verses that starts right at that worry. It opens with an oath.
The Arabic word is al-asr, time; Pickthall puts it, "By the declining day." Then the verdict, with no warm-up: "Lo! man is in a state of loss."

teach.b: Then the way out, in the same breath: "Save those who believe and do good works, and exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to endurance." Three verses, and four parts to a life not lost.
Look at the last two. They aren't things you do alone. They're things you do to one another.
There's a story about what that looked like.
The commentator Ibn Kathir records a report that when two of the Prophet's companions met, they wouldn't part until one had recited this surah to the other, and then they'd say salaam.

And the jurist al-Shafi'i, tradition says, held that if people reflected on this one surah, it would be enough for them. So, in this surah, time is something God swears by, and its loss isn't fixed by a better schedule.
It's answered by faith, by good deeds, and by people who tell each other the truth and help each other hold on.
One more to pass on: al-asr is also the name of the afternoon prayer, said as the day begins to decline. Half of what keeps a life from loss, in this surah, needs another person.

how: Surah al-Asr is among the short surahs Muslims learn and recite in prayer; its name, al-asr, is also the name of the afternoon prayer.

o: an oath by time: loss, unless faith, good and urging truth
a rule to pray at one set hour every single afternoon
a warning that the world will end one day at sunset

games.q: Surah al-Asr, part by part: tap the pairs.
p: where people are, says verse two
said this surah would be enough

s: Surah al-Asr is advice on managing your schedule
it answers loss with faith, good works, and urging one another to truth and endurance.
two of the four ways out of loss are done with other people
exhort one another to truth, and exhort one another to endurance.
the word asr also names one of the daily prayers
the afternoon prayer, as the day begins to decline.

games.q: a friend keeps missing deadlines and you've noticed. in Surah al-Asr's terms, what fits best?
o: tell her the truth kindly, and help her hold on; that's urged one to another.
say nothing; the surah is about her own deeds, not yours to mention.
send her a time-management app; the surah is about wasted hours.
games.why: verse three: exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to endurance. truth and patience travel together.

practice: Take the next hour. Name one good use for it, then the one thing most likely to swallow it, then what you'll do when that thing shows up. Say all three to yourself plainly, and sit with the hour in front of you.

wordCard.voice: By time: the oath that opens Surah al-Asr, three verses on a life that isn't lost.

orig.note: Arabic: time, the declining day; also the name of the afternoon prayer.

carryVoice: Worth keeping: by time, and never alone, with truth and patience. Two of seven from the Quran.

sources.q: Lo! man is in a state of loss
